title: When the heart is true
hook: truth is known when the heart is true and falsehood's dirt is washed (Asa di Var, ang 468)

segments.voice: Yesterday, koorh: the false king, everything that passes. Today the very next salok answers it with its opposite: sach, truth.

A friend who's being straight with you shows it, and not only in the words. The eyes stay on yours, the shoulders aren't braced, there's no little gap between what's said and what's meant. The opposite shows too, even when every word is technically accurate. Truth isn't only a property of sentences. It's a property of people. Guru Nanak's salok right after the list of koorh doesn't ask what is true. It asks something harder: when can a person be said to know truth at all?
screen: `A FRIEND BEING STRAIGHT WITH YOU.` → `TRUTH LIVES IN PEOPLE.` → `WHEN DOES A PERSON KNOW IT?`

segments.voice: The salok on ang 468 is built like a ladder, each rung starting the same way: sach taa par jaaneeai. Truth is known only when. Then Guru Nanak fills in the rest. Truth is known when the heart itself is true. When the dirt of falsehood comes off, and the body is washed clean. Truth is known when a person loves truth, when hearing the Name the mind delights, and so finds the door of freedom. Truth is known when a person knows the way to live: making the body a field and planting the Creator's seed in it. Truth is known when a person takes true teaching, shows kindness to living beings, and gives what they can. Truth is known when a person makes their own self the place of pilgrimage, and settles there, guided by the True Guru. And the last rung: truth is the medicine for everyone. It washes out wrongdoing. Look at what this list is made of. Not one rung is about winning an argument or holding the right opinion. Every rung is about a person: what the heart loves, how the life is lived, how the hands treat other beings. In Gurbani, sach is both a name for the One and the quality of a life lined up with the One. So a true heart isn't one that never makes mistakes. It's a heart with no gap between what it shows and what it is. Yesterday's salok said koorh drowns boatloads. Today's says truth heals everyone. The washing comes first, and it's daily work.
screen: `TRUTH IS KNOWN ONLY WHEN...` · `THE HEART ITSELF IS TRUE.` · `THE BODY A FIELD, THE SEED PLANTED.` · `TRUTH IS MEDICINE FOR ALL.` · then, large: `A TRUE HEART.`

segments.voice: Look gently for one small gap between what you show and what is: a white lie you've repeated, a version of yourself you've been performing. Pick just one and picture washing it, the way you'd wash dirt off your hands. If you pray, say Waheguru.
Sach, truth: Guru Nanak's ladder says sach is known only when the heart is true, falsehood's dirt is washed, and the life is lived in kindness.
Your line: a true heart. No gap between what it shows and what it is. Day five hundred forty-nine, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear this salok of truth in the dawn singing of Asa di Var, and Sikhs often recall Guru Nanak's line in Sri Rag that truth stands above all, and truthful living higher still.

sources.ref: Asa di Var, salok M1 (sach taa par jaaneeai), Ang 468

notes: The salok is paraphrased; confirm the five rungs (true heart and washing; love of truth and the Name; the body as a field with the Creator's seed; true teaching, compassion and giving; the self as pilgrimage place under the True Guru) and the closing 'truth is medicine for all'.
The phrase 'truthful living matters even more than knowing the truth' in howItsDone echoes Sri Rag M1 ('sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar', Ang 62) without quoting; confirm the framing.

Fresh review: myth said every line begins 'sach taa par jaaneeai', but the refrain opens each couplet, not each line; now 'each rung'. Hook no longer tells the listener what they can tell; howItsDone now points to the Sri Rag line rather than a loose paraphrase.
